title: Tame inertia implies a surjective group trace
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let a finite group $G$ act on $R$ by ring automorphisms. Write $A=R^G=\{r\in R:g(r)=r\text{ for all }g\in G\}$. For each prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$, let $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=R_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and define its inertia subgroup by $I_{\mathfrak p}=\{g\in G:g(\mathfrak p)=\mathfrak p\text{ and }g\text{ induces the identity on }\kappa(\mathfrak p)\}$. Assume $|I_{\mathfrak p}|$ is invertible in $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ for every prime $\mathfrak p$. Then the $A$-linear group trace $T:R\to A$, $T(r)=\sum_{g\in G}g(r)$, is surjective; equivalently, there is $a\in R$ with $\sum_{g\in G}g(a)=1$. No Noetherian or finite-type hypothesis is imposed.
